post.summary:
Upload a bank file (OFX, QFX, QBO or CSV; the format is read from the
content). Its rows are staged, each with what it would become, and
suggestions are made: the account of a statement that has none, and every
row's labels (docs/ai.md). Nothing enters the ledger until the import is
committed.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description:
The account the file is for, if the client knows: used when the file
names none (a CSV) or a number no account has. Without it, such a
statement waits for its account in review. Refused for a file with
several statements.

parameters.description: The file's name, to recognize the import by.

requestBody.description: The file, as is (at most 10 MiB)

post.summary:
Commit the imports you saw as ready, oldest first, each on its own, as
[`commit`] does. Each is checked again just before: one that's gone, no
longer ready (committing another may have changed it), or changed since
is skipped, as is one commit refuses; the others go ahead.

get.summary:
Get one staged import, with its statements and how many rows have each
status.

delete.summary: Discard a staged import: nothing of it enters the ledger.

post.summary:
Commit the import: all or nothing. Every row's status is worked out
again first; if any changed (the ledger moved on since), nothing is
committed and the import comes back with a 409 to review again. Then each
row's decision is carried out: new transactions go into one `file`
import batch; transfer matches turn the matched transaction into a
transfer; every row that's now in the ledger is recorded as imported, so
the same row is a duplicate next time, and what this file says about it is
kept with its transaction (once per file, whatever its name). Each
statement's ledger balance becomes a balance check. The staged import is
then gone.

409.description: A statement has no account, a row's status changed, or a month is closed

422.description: A row breaks a ledger rule

post.summary:
Work an import out again without uploading it again: its rows' statuses
against the ledger, the suggestions that aren't confident (the
statement's account, then each row's labels; yours and confident ones
stay) and transfer matches across every staged import.

The household pool for one month: shared income and expenses, stipends,

The active rules script (the newest version); version 0, empty, when

put.summary:
Upload a new version of the rules script. It's compiled and every name
it uses is checked against the ledger; an invalid script is refused with
its errors, by line (`rules-invalid`), and never becomes active. A valid
one is active at once, for the next file uploaded.

post.summary:
What a script would set for the ledger's transactions in a date range
(those between one of your accounts and the outside, as an imported row
becomes), compared with what they have. Runs the active script, or a
candidate given in the body (validated first); stores nothing. The
bank's own fields (`row.raw`) are empty here, and `fn account` isn't run.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day (at most about three years after `from`).

Statements for a range of months, without their lines: the history used

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last month, `YYYY-MM` (at most 120 months in all).

get.summary: A month's parameters (its own, or carried forward) and whether it's closed.

put.summary:
Set a month's stipends and funders. `If-Match` is the ETag from GET
(`"0"` for a month never set).

409.description: The month is closed, or no USD commodity yet

post.summary:
Close a month: edits to transactions dated in it are refused until it's
reopened. Needs every person's stipend and every business's funder set
for the month itself.
Reopen a closed month. Always allowed (design §4.4).

get.summary:
The month's statement: each edge's claims, stipend, due, paid,
outstanding and lines (design §4.3). Always computed from current data.

Measure a local AI method, alone or with remote AI after it, on the
ledger's own past (docs/ai.md). For each month, the method learns from
everything before it, then suggests labels for the month's transactions
(between one of your accounts and the outside) as if they were being
imported, and an account for each account's transactions; remote AI, if
asked, is shown what's before the month and asked about what the method
left unsure. The guesses are compared with the ledger. Reads only;
nothing is stored.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last month, `YYYY-MM`; `from` if omitted (at most 24 months in all).

parameters.name: method
parameters.description:
The local method to measure, as configured (`lexical-knn-v2`); the
server's own if omitted.

parameters.name: remote
parameters.description:
Also ask remote AI, as configured, about what the method leaves
unsure (at most 3 months). Its requests are real ones, billed.

candidates.description: For a mismatch, on a single check only.

value_in_id.description: The commodity values are in, when asked.

Guesses by confidence: those from `from` up to the next bin's `from`

Ceremony.description: A ceremony started: hand `options` to the browser.

Decision.description: What committing does with a row.

DecisionSuggestion.description: What matching suggests committing does with a row.

token.description: Shown only once: store it in the token file.

changed.description: Those it would label differently from the ledger.

items.description: Changed and failed rows, by date (at most 500).

labeled.description: Of them, those it set any label for.

rows.description:

version.description: The script's version; absent for a candidate.

One edge of the settlement tree (a child and its parent) for one month.

carried.description:
`outstanding` at the end of the previous month: past differences,

claims.description: Regular claims across the edge this month.

outstanding.description:

paid.description: Regular payments that settle this month.

Where a transaction came from outside Exchequer, such as its ID in the

name.description: What to call the passkey, e.g. `iPhone`.

near duplicate never is). Needs work.

unlabeled.description:
New rows with a label neither chosen nor confidently suggested.
Needs work.

ReadinessState.description:
How close an import is to committing (design §6.7): `ready` commits as
shown, with nothing left to a guess (a rule's suggestion is yours);
`suggested` would commit too, on confident AI suggestions you haven't
confirmed; `needs_work` needs you first.

ReadyOutcome.description: What committing one of the ready imports did.

skipped.description:
Why it wasn't committed: gone, no longer ready, changed since it was
checked, or refused.

to.description: Default (and at most): today in the server's time zone.

Refreshed.description: A refresh: running, or how it went.

errors.description:
`source: what went wrong`, for each failure; the next source was
asked instead.

sources.description: The configured sources, in the order asked.

Row.description:
One row. A grouped field is present (`null` for "none", e.g. no
category); a field not grouped by is absent.

amount.description: At the commodity's precision. Positive: into your accounts.

RowCounts.description: How many rows have each status.

RowSplit.description:
One part of a row split before commit: a split of the new transaction
between the statement's account and this part's other side.

amount.description: Positive; the parts add up to the row's amount, unsigned.

category_id.description:
Absent: none. Not for a transfer (unless between a liquid and a
non-liquid account).

counterparty_id.description:
Who's on the other side; with neither this nor
`transfer_account_id`, outside the household, unknown who.

purpose_id.description:
Absent: the account's owner (the household, between a liquid and a
non-liquid account). Not for a transfer.

transfer_account_id.description: The other side when it's one of your accounts.

RowUpdate.description: Fields to change; omitted ones stay as they are, `null` clears one.

oneOf.description: `null`: back to the default for the row's status.

revert.description:
Labels to stop choosing, so their suggestions apply again. Setting a
label (to a value or `null`) makes it your choice.

splits.description:
Split the row into these parts (two or more, adding up to its
amount), each a split of the new transaction; `null` or `[]`: not
split. Only for a row added as new that isn't a transfer match; a
split row can't change its decision until the parts are cleared.

transfer_account_id.description:
One of your accounts as the other side: the row is a transfer. It
sets the counterparty label (as yours), so not with
`counterparty_id`; `null` is the same as `counterparty_id: null`.

RuleScript.description: A version of the rules script.

author.description: The name of the token that uploaded it.

version.description: 0 when there's none yet: no rules.

note.description: Why, like a commit message (at most 500 characters).

source.description: The whole script; empty for no rules.

Score.description: Guesses against what the ledger says.

confident.description: Guesses at 900 or more, which commit would take.

confident_only.description: Over guesses at 900 or more only.

guessed.description: Of them, those with a guess.

Session.description: A browser signed in: send `token` as the bearer token until it expires.

params_from.description:
The month these parameters were set for: this one, an earlier one
they're carried forward from, or absent when none were ever set.

funders.description: Businesses left out are funded by the household.

SkippedLine.description: A line of the file that wasn't read.

kind.description:
Read-only. Money between a liquid and a non-liquid account is an
expense (into it) or income (out of it).

SplitPointer.description: One split, by its transaction and position.

amount.description: Signed from the account's side: negative is money leaving it.

chosen.description: The labels you set (a `null` one is an explicit none).

counterparty_id.description:
The labels below are what a new transaction gets: your choice, else a
confident suggestion. For a new transaction: who's on the outside
side (unknown if absent and there's no `transfer_account_id`).

decided.description: Whether `decision` is the client's choice rather than the default.

oneOf.description:
What committing does with the row: the client's choice, else the
default for its status. Absent while the statement has no account.

match_transaction_id.description: The existing transaction a duplicate or transfer duplicate is of.

missing.description:
For a row that will be a new transaction: the labels that are
neither yours nor confidently suggested. Commit refuses while any row
has some.

native_id.description: The bank's own ID for the row, if it has one.

not_applicable.description:
Labels that don't apply: a transfer's category and purpose (design
§3.2).

purpose_id.description: Who the money was for; absent, the account's owner.

raw.description: The row's fields as the file had them.

set_description.description: The new transaction's description, if not the bank's.

splits.description:
The row split into parts, each a split of the new transaction; empty
if it isn't split. A split row is added as new, and its labels are
the parts': the row's own, and its suggestions, don't apply.

oneOf.description:
What matching suggests `decision` be; absent while the statement has
no account.

suggestions.description: At most one per label, confident or not.

transfer_account_id.description:
The other side when it's one of your accounts: the row is a transfer,
whose category and purpose don't apply (unless one account is liquid
and the other isn't: an expense or income).
A transfer match's is its other side's account.

oneOf.description:
For a transfer match: the staged row that is the transfer's other
side.

StagedStatement.description: One account's part of the file.

account_id.description:
The account the rows are worked out against: the one the file's
number belongs to, or the client's choice, else a confident suggestion
(`account_suggested`). `null` until there is one.

account_suggested.description: Whether `account_id` is the suggestion's, not yet the statement's own.

number_last4.description: The last four of the account number in the file (CSVs have none).

oneOf.description:
A suggested account, confident or not; it stays after you pick one,
to record how good it was.

client.description: What the CLI calls itself, shown to the approver: `cli on laptop`.

fetching.description:
Missing or stale prices are being fetched: asked again shortly, the
figures may be fresher.

unpriced.description: Splits left out because they have no value in USD.

account_id.description: The account the statement is for; `null` to unset it.

remember_number.description:
Also add the file's account number to the account, so its next
files resolve by themselves.

Stipend.description: What the Household owes a person for the month.

Suggester.description: The exact system that made a suggestion.

details.description: What else identifies it, e.g. the data a local model learned from.

name.description: E.g. the rules, a local method, or a remote deployment and model.

SuggesterKind.description: Which level of the suggestion stack made a suggestion (docs/ai.md).

expires_at.description: When a session stops working; other tokens last until revoked.

user_id.description: The user it belongs to; none for a script's token.

import_batch_id.description: Read-only: the import batch the transaction entered with.

file_name.description: Its file's name, if it was given.

Unpriced.description:
A split the settlement couldn't value: neither leg is in USD, and no
price connects its commodity to USD.

User.description: A household member who signs in.

ValuationOut.description: What one commodity was worth in another, and which prices say so.

derived.description: Chained through another commodity, not one price.

prices.description: One price, or two chained through a pivot commodity (`derived`).

provisional.description: Uses a price for a day still in progress.

stale.description: No price close enough to the date: the newest older one was used.

fetching.description:
Missing or stale prices are being fetched: asked again shortly, the
answer may be fresher.

Valued.description: A valuation, and whether fresher prices for it are being fetched.

schema.description:
Newest schema migration built into this server. Backups record it so
a restore can check compatibility (design §14.2).
